description: Three outlets disagree both on the cause of a building collapse and on the number of people injured.

event.title: Partial building collapse under investigation
event.description: Sources disagree on the cause and casualty count of a partial building collapse.

articles.title: Engineers say age-related structural failure likely cause of collapse
articles.summary: Independent engineers cited by this outlet attribute the collapse to structural failure due to the building's age; 5 injured reported.
articles.raw_content: Independent structural engineers consulted by this outlet said the partial collapse of the downtown building was likely caused by age-related structural failure, noting the building was constructed over 80 years ago. Five people were reported injured, none critically.

articles.title: City engineer points to recent renovation work as likely cause
articles.summary: The city's chief engineer, quoted directly, says ongoing renovation work is a more likely cause than the building's age.
articles.raw_content: The city's chief structural engineer, quoted directly, said recent renovation work at the site is a more likely cause of the collapse than the building's age alone, citing modifications made to load-bearing walls in the past year. The engineer did not rule out age as a contributing factor.

articles.title: Eight injured in building collapse, fire department says
articles.summary: The fire department's official injury count is eight, higher than the five reported elsewhere.
articles.raw_content: The fire department's official count puts the number of people injured in the building collapse at eight, higher than earlier reports. All eight were transported to area hospitals; none of the injuries are reported as life-threatening.

must_preserve_facts: There is disagreement about the cause: structural age (source 81) vs. recent renovation work (source 82)
There is disagreement about the injury count: 5 (source 81) vs. 8 (source 83, official fire department count)
must_not_invent: A single definitive official cause (none of the sources agree, and no final determination is reported)
A single definitive injury count presented without noting the discrepancy
known_ambiguities: Both the cause and the casualty count are genuinely disputed across sources, not just reported with varying detail. The cause claim and the injury-count claim should likely each be tagged 'disputed', since they represent direct, substantive disagreement rather than mere evolving/unconfirmed reporting.
validation_notes: Exercises validateClaimComparisons' status enum and source attribution across 3 distinct source_ids (81, 82, 83). A model that picks only one cause or one injury count without surfacing the disagreement would be a quality failure invisible to the schema validator, which only checks structural validity and article/source ID grounding.
